title: Functional vs Class Components
definition: Functional components are simple JavaScript functions that accept props and return JSX. Class components are ES6 classes that extend React.Component and require a render() method.
simpleExplanation: Imagine building a chair. A Class component is like a complex factory assembly line with a manual you have to read (constructors, 'this' keyword, lifecycle methods). A Functional component is like a simple 3D printer: you give it a design (props), and it prints the chair (JSX). Before 2019, only the factory (Class) could remember things (State). Now, thanks to Hooks, the 3D printer can do everything the factory can do, but with way less headache.
realWorldExample: If you look at an old 2017 React codebase, you will see `class App extends React.Component`. You will see `this.state = {}` and `this.handleClick.bind(this)`. In modern React, you will exclusively see `function App()` and `const [state, setState] = useState()`.
useCases: Functional Components: The modern standard for building 99% of all React UI.
Class Components: Maintaining legacy codebases, or specifically building an Error Boundary (which currently requires a Class).

answers.question: Can you use Hooks inside a Class Component?
answers.answer: No. Hooks were specifically designed to solve the problems of Class components. They are strictly for Functional components.

answers.question: Why did React shift away from Class components?
answers.answer: Classes required understanding the confusing `this` keyword, required binding event handlers manually, and made it very difficult to reuse stateful logic (forcing developers to use complex patterns like HOCs or Render Props). Hooks solved all of this elegantly.

answers.question: Are Functional components actually faster?
answers.answer: Not necessarily. While they avoid the overhead of instantiating an ES6 Class, the performance difference is negligible in most apps. The shift was primarily about Developer Experience (DX) and code reusability, not raw speed.
